clue.text: What dogs might do behind multi-coloured birds

indicators.note: the dogs' action sits behind, so after, the colour word in the answer

parts.note: pied means marked in patches of two or more colours
a happy dog wags its tail, so dogs wag tails

explanation.surface: A picture of dogs trotting along behind a flock of colourful birds.
explanation.definitionFit: The pied wagtail is a common black-and-white British songbird that constantly bobs its tail.

clue.text: Feel bitter about following papa here

indicators.note: the bitterness word comes after the papa letter in the answer

parts.note: P is Papa in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to resent something is to feel bitter about it

explanation.surface: Someone sulking because they have to trail after their father.
explanation.walkthrough: 'here' looks like a throwaway word at the end, but it is the whole definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being present means being in attendance at this place, so the adjective stands for here.

clue.text: Planet's core — hot from top to bottom

indicators.note: the H for hot at the start of the word is shifted from the top of this down entry to its foot

parts.note: the heart of something is its core or centre

explanation.surface: A geology note: a planet's core is hot right through from top to bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the top is the first letter, so moving H from top to bottom sends it to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth is the third planet from the Sun, the one we live on.

clue.text: Reflect on well-rounded learner driver leaving A1

parts.note: to wonder about something is to reflect on it

indicators.note: the learner letter departs from the rounded word, so it is taken out

parts.note: full in the sense of plump or rounded in figure
L is the learner plate on a British learner driver's car

explanation.surface: A learner driver, having finished pondering, pulls off the A1 road.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 is Britain's longest road, which the surface plays on; here it means first-rate.
explanation.definitionFit: A1 is an informal term for excellent, top-class, which matches wonderful.

clue.text: Convict upset going round old prison

indicators.note: the reversed convict word wraps around the letter for old
in a down clue upset turns the convict word upside down, so it reads backwards

parts.note: an old lag is a slang term for a convict

explanation.surface: An upset prisoner pacing round an old jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaol is the traditional British spelling of jail, a prison.

clue.text: Satisfied we snared criminal

indicators.note: the letters are treated in a criminal, crooked way and so rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Police pleased that they have trapped a criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' looks like the person snared, but it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A question or need that has been answered has been met or fulfilled, i.e. satisfied.

clue.text: Unimportant plane trip taking off loudly

indicators.note: the letter for loudly is removed, playing on a plane taking off

parts.note: a flight is a journey by plane
F is forte, the musical direction for loudly

explanation.surface: A short hop of a plane journey, taking off with a roar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking off' reads as part of the flight scene but signals removal.
explanation.definitionFit: Light reading or a light matter is trivial and not serious, hence unimportant.

clue.text: Broadcast about the French Resistance in heroic exploit

indicators.note: the three short pieces are placed inside the exploit word

parts.note: a deed is a notable act or exploit
C is circa, Latin for about
la is the French feminine for the
R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A radio report about a heroic act by the French Resistance in wartime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the French Resistance' looks like one name, but splits into the French and Resistance.
explanation.definitionFit: To broadcast something is to make it widely known, i.e. to have declared it publicly.

clue.text: Tango calms guys

definitions.note: a verb here: guys means mocks

parts.note: T is Tango in the NATO phonetic alphabet
eases means soothes or calms

explanation.surface: A slow dance that calms a group of men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guys' looks like a plural noun for men; it is the verb to guy, to make fun of.
explanation.definitionFit: To guy someone is an old-fashioned verb for ridiculing them, the same as teasing.

clue.text: Wrong about returning euros — no exchanges

indicators.note: the short word for about comes back, read in the opposite direction

parts.note: re means concerning or about

indicators.note: the letters are swapped around, as currencies are exchanged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bureau de change wrongly says no euros are coming back and no exchanges can be made.
explanation.definitionFit: Erroneous describes something containing an error, so incorrect or mistaken.

clue.text: Environmentalist cut holding black bird

indicators.note: the shortened word wraps around the black letter
the environmentalist word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a Green is a member of an environmental party
B is the pencil-grade abbreviation for black

explanation.surface: A conservationist with a short haircut cradling a black bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The grebe is a diving waterbird, such as the great crested grebe.

clue.text: Parrots from Spain caught by homes miles away

definitions.note: a verb here: parrots means repeats

parts.note: E is the international vehicle registration for Spain (España)
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: the miles letter is sent away from the homes word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Parrots imported from Spain found in houses far from anywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parrots' looks like birds, but it is the verb meaning to repeat mindlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: To echo someone is to repeat their words back, exactly as a parrot mimics speech.

clue.text: Record temperature inside irritates snakes?

indicators.note: the record and temperature letters go inside the irritates word

parts.note: riles means annoys or irritates
an EP is an extended-play record
T is the standard symbol for temperature

explanation.surface: A record temperature inside a reptile house riles the snakes.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that snakes are only one example of the class.
explanation.definitionFit: Snakes belong to the reptiles, so the plural word is a definition by example.

clue.text: Disturb what golfer may do

definitions.meaning: first meaning: slang for to annoy or irritate
second meaning: a golfer tees off by striking the first shot from the tee

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to irritate someone and to play the opening drive of a golf hole.

clue.text: Current in intense changes creating bright spark

indicators.note: the current symbol goes inside the rearranged letters
changes means the letters of intense are rearranged

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Electricity running through something that changes intensely makes a spark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' makes EINSTEN from INTENSE, and I goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Einstein is used for any genius, and a bright spark is a clever person.

clue.text: For each class, son behaves

parts.note: per means for each, as in per person
a form is a school class

explanation.surface: A school report on how each class, and one son, behaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Performs here means acts or functions, as a machine or pupil performs well, i.e. behaves.

clue.text: Around king, Harry often got neglected

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the king letter
to harry is to harass, so the letters are harassed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
R is Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Prince Harry often found himself left out around the King.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like the prince next to a king, but it is the verb to harass, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something forgotten has been overlooked or left unattended, i.e. neglected.

clue.text: Big cat scratching tail on temple for the gods

indicators.note: the big cat's last letter is struck out, scratched off its tail

parts.note: a panther is a big cat, a leopard or jaguar
taken as written

explanation.surface: A big cat scratching its tail on the stones of an ancient temple.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantheon, from Greek for all gods, is a temple dedicated to every deity, like the one in Rome.

clue.text: Large ruptures after family tragedy

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come after the family word

parts.note: kin are one's family or relatives

indicators.note: the word large is ruptured, broken up and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A family suffers big rifts and a tragedy follows.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's family feud fits the play, in which Lear's family is torn apart.
explanation.definitionFit: King Lear is Shakespeare's tragedy of an old king betrayed by two of his daughters.

clue.text: This could make you peek — go on!

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read as an instruction: put the word ..., i.e. reverse it in a down light, and it reads peek
second meaning: ... as encouragement to continue

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a reverse clue: the answer is an instruction, and following it on the word keep in a down entry gives peek.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep up is to continue at the same pace, so it urges someone to carry on.

clue.text: Rush back with ecstasy and initially reimburse dealer

indicators.note: the rush word is read backwards

parts.note: to dart is to rush
E is the street abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

indicators.note: only the first letter of the following word is used

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A drug dealer has to hurry back with ecstasy and repay someone first.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface paints a drug dealer, but the definition is a plain merchant.
explanation.definitionFit: A trader buys and sells goods for profit, so is a dealer.

clue.text: Animal, embarrassed, pulled up grass

parts.note: an embarrassed person turns red

indicators.note: in a down clue the grass word is turned upward, so read backwards

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass

explanation.surface: An animal, red-faced, tugging up a mouthful of grass.
explanation.definitionFit: The red deer is the largest native British wild mammal, a large deer species.

clue.text: China follows website regularly I guess

indicators.note: the China word follows the other pieces
only every other letter of website is used, the 2nd, 4th and 6th

parts.note: taken as written
the clue's I is used just as it stands, as a single letter
in Cockney rhyming slang, china plate means mate, a friend

explanation.surface: A friend checks a website at intervals and makes a guess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country; in Cockney rhyming slang china (plate) is a mate.
explanation.definitionFit: An estimate is an approximate calculation or judgement, a rough guess.

clue.text: Former Prime Minister became vacuous possibly

parts.note: Theresa May was UK Prime Minister from 2016 to 2019

indicators.note: the word became is emptied of its middle, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A former PM who possibly became empty-headed in office.
explanation.definitionFit: Maybe is an adverb of uncertainty, the same as perhaps or possibly.

clue.text: Tricked female rejected John and Edward

indicators.note: the toilet word is turned back, read in reverse

parts.note: john is slang for a toilet, as is loo
Ed is the short form of Edward

explanation.surface: A woman spurned John and Edward after tricking them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John' looks like a man's name beside Edward, but it is slang for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: To be fooled is to be deceived or duped, i.e. tricked.

clue.text: Found adult leaves meal

indicators.note: the adult letter leaves, so is removed

parts.note: to found a business is to launch it
A is the old film-certificate abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A grown-up walks out of a meal they set up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' looks like the past of find; it is the verb to establish.
explanation.definitionFit: Lunch is the midday meal.

clue.text: Relaxed politician supporting Liberal one

indicators.note: in a down light the politician sits beneath, so supports, the other letters

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An easygoing MP backing a single Liberal colleague.
explanation.definitionFit: Limp means slack or floppy, lacking stiffness, which is a sense of relaxed.

clue.text: Somewhat fun if you join together

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the phrase are used, so the answer is concealed within it

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An invitation: it is quite fun if you come together with others.
explanation.definitionFit: To unify is to bring things into one, to unite or join them together.

clue.text: Being sixteen — excited with constant energy

indicators.note: the letters of sixteen are stirred up and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
c is the physics constant for the speed of light
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Being sixteen means being excited and full of constant energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being' looks like a verb opening the sentence; it is a noun meaning life itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Being as a noun is the state of living or existing, i.e. existence.

clue.text: One enjoys saving writer in front of New York thief?

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument, so a writer
to pinch is slang for to steal, so a pincher is a thief

explanation.surface: A New York author who is also a thief, but enjoys putting money by.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that pincher for thief is an invented word.
explanation.definitionFit: A penny-pincher is a miserly person who hates spending and so loves saving money.
